previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of liver transplant, alcoholic cirrhosis, and chronic malnutrition, was transferred from an outside hospital intubated due to hypoxic respiratory failure and healthcare-associated pneumonia caused by multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. He was treated with intravenous vancomycin, meropenem, and amikacin, which was later de-escalated based on culture results. After successful extubation, a video swallow study revealed aspiration, leading to dietary modifications with soft solids and thin liquids using specific techniques to reduce aspiration risk. His chronic pain regimen was adjusted with oxycodone discontinued and oxycontin initiated. Sirolimus was reduced to 2 mg daily due to elevated levels, and iron supplementation was stopped due to iron overload on liver biopsy. He was discharged home with services on room air, with prescriptions for albuterol nebulizer, supplemental oxygen as needed, and follow-up with speech therapy and transplant clinic.

Brief Hospital Course:
Patient is a ___ yo male with PMH of orthotopic liver transplant 
in ___, complicated by multiple infections (pna) and chronic 
diarrhea, recent hospitalization for pna (dischaged ___ 
admitted with hypoxia and fever found to have multifocal 
pneumonia and UTI ___ MDR psuedomonas. 

#Pneumonia: Patient had signs and symptoms of pneuoonia, 
including fever, hypoxia, cough. CXR and CT were also consistent 
with pneumonia. Initially there was concern for aspiration 
pneumonia as he endorsed gagging 2 nights prior to admission. He 
was started on vancomycin and meropenem for hospital acquired 
pneumonia. His sputum cultures revealed psuedomonas sensitive to 
meropenem and vancomycin was stopped.  A video swallow study was 
performed and there was no evidence of aspiration, he was 
continued on soft solids and thin liquids. He will be treated 
with a total of 14 days of meropenem to be continued until 
___.

#Urinary tract infection: patient has chronic indwelling foley 
and is at risk for urinary tract infections. His UA was 
consistent with UTI. His foley was draining frank put and was 
changed. His urine culture revealed pseudomas sensitive to 
meropenem, which is was on for his pneumonia. 

# Hx of Liver tranplant: patient had elevated AST, ALT and Alk 
phos on admission which trended down and were normal on 
discharge. His LFTs were likely initially elevated in the 
setting of acute illness. His rapamycin levels were elevated 
during this admission and his dose was decreased from 2 mg po 
once a day to 1.5 mg po once a day and then finally to 1 mg po 
once a day on dischage. 

___: Patient was admitted with increased creatinine to 1.6 (1.3 
at last hospitalization and 1.0 prior) which improved with iv 
fluids and was 1.0 on discharge.

#Anemia: patient has chronic anemia, possibly related to 
malnutrition. baseline hct ___. His HCT fluctuated between 24 
and 29. He required one unit of PRBCs for HCT of 22.7. His 
hematocrit was stable on disharge. 

#Nutrition: Patient has chronic malnutrition and he receives 
tube feeds for nutrition. He was evaluated by speech & swallow 
and he had a normal video swallow. He was initially keep NPO 
except tube feeds but his diet was then changed to soft solids 
and thin liquids. He was continued on thiamine, vit D & calcium.

#Leukocytopenia: Patient had normal WBC on admission but then 
developed leukopenia with a WBC of 2.9. The etiology of his 
leukopenia is unclear. CMV viral load was not detectable. 

#Chronic Diarrhea: at baseline. His had no abdominal pain or 
leukocytosis to suggest GI infection. 

#Chronic pain: stable, he was continued home fentanyl patch, 
oxycodone SR, hydromorphone prn

#Cervical Stenosis: Patient had a history of cervical stenosis. 
CT chest showed focal kyphosis. Plain C-spine x-rays were 
obtained and were unrevealing. Dedicated C-spine CT can be 
obtained as outpatient if clinically warranted. 

#Depression/ insomnia: He was continued on his home mirtazapine 
and amitryptyline.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Fever, hypoxia and vomiting.

COMPARISON:  ___.

PA AND LATERAL VIEWS OF THE CHEST:  Nasogastric tube tip courses below the
diaphragm, off the inferior borders of the film.  The heart size is moderately
enlarged.  The aorta remains mildly tortuous.  Ill-defined opacities within
the left lung continue to improve.  More focal opacity within the lateral
aspect of the right lung base appears slightly worse in the interval. There is
persistent collapse of the right lower lobe.  There is a small right pleural
effusion.  No pneumothorax is present.  Previous pattern of pulmonary vascular
congestion has continued to improve.

IMPRESSION:  Ill-defined opacities in the left lung appear slightly improved
when compared to prior, which may reflect an improving infectious etiology
versus asymmetric pulmonary edema.  More focal ill-defined opacity within the
right lung base may represent an area of atelectasis but infection is not
excluded.  Right lower lobe collapse is unchanged.  Small right pleural
effusion.

INDICATION:  ___ with pneumonia.  Evaluate for interval change.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior chest radiographs from ___ to ___, CT of the torso ___, and CT of the abdomen, ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector helical scanning of the chest was performed without
intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformats were displayed.

NON-CONTRAST CT OF THE CHEST:  There is moderate centrilobular emphysema.  The
right lower lobe is completely collapsed, with heterogeneous attenuation. 
Previously, the right lower lobe showed chronic atelectasis in a rounded
configuration.  The further collapse of this lobe and heterogeneous
attenuation are suggestive of a combination of atelectasis and pneumonia
currently.  There is thickening of the right pleura, a small right pleural
effusion, and expansion of the  extrapleural fat, likely from chronic
inflammation.  There are secretions within the right lower lobe bronchus.  In
the posterior aspect of the right upper lobe, there is dense dependent
consolidation, highly suggestive of aspiration pneumonia.  Within the left
lower lobe, there is also extensive consolidation and a small pleural
effusion.  Finally, there are scattered small peripheral nodules in the
dependent location in the left upper lobe, which are also likely infectious.  

Low density of intracardiac blood likely reflects anemia.  There are extensive
coronary artery calcifications.  No significant mediastinal adenopathy.  NG
tube enters the stomach and courses out of the field of view.  The patient is
status post liver transplant.  Evaluation of the upper abdomen is limited due
to lack of contrast, however, there is splenomegaly and probable varices.  

There are no concerning lytic or sclerotic lesions.  Anterior cervical fusion
(partially imaged) extends from C6 through T1.  There is separation of the
plate from the vertebral column superiorly (around C6-C7), and posterior
inflection of the lower plate into the vertebral body at T1.  There is focal
kyphosis at this level of approximately 15 degrees.  This finding is new
compared to CT of the torso from ___. 

IMPRESSION:
1.  Extensive multifocal pneumonia, worse in the lower lobes bilaterally and
in the dependent portion of the right upper lobe, and which may be due to
aspiration.  There is progression of chronic right lower lobe atelectasis with
complete collapse of the right lower lobe and secretions in the right lower
lobe bronchus.

2.  Focal kyphosis in the cervical spine due to separation of the ACDF fusion
plate from the vertebral column superiorly and posterior inflection of the
lower plate at T1.  Recommend cervical spine radiographs for better
evaluation.  

Findings and recommendations were discussed with Dr. ___ at 9:45 ___ on

INDICATION:  Patient who is status post liver transplant, readmitted for
pneumonia.

VIDEO OROPHARYNGEAL SWALLOW:  The study was conducted in collaboration with
speech pathology.  Various consistencies of barium were administered by mouth
including thin, nectar, puree, and ground.  There is a solitary episode of
penetration with nectar consistency.  There is penetration with thin
consistency.  There is no penetration or aspiration with puree or ground
consistency.  There is mild retention in the valleculae with nectar, puree,
and ground.

IMPRESSION:  No aspiration.

Please refer to the complete report from speech pathology that is available on
CareWeb.

HISTORY:  Multifocal pneumonia.  Incidental kyphosis seen on CT.

CERVICAL SPINE, THREE VIEWS INCLUDING SWIMMER'S VIEW.  Additional views are
not labeled, but appear to be flexion/extension.  

An NG tube is in place.  There is osteometallic fusion of the lower cervical
spine at the C5-7 levels, with anterior plate and screws and presumed
intervening bone graft.  The plate does not clearly lie flush with the
anterior cortex of the bones.  Lower levels of the cervical spine are not well
seen due to overlying anatomy. However, at C2-4, vertebral body and disc
heights are preserved.  

There is good range of motion in flexion and mild-to-moderate range of motion
in extension.  On flexion, there is minimal anterolisthesis (approximately 2.8
mm) of C4/C5 which appears to reduce in neutral and extension views.  No other
evidence of abnormal motion is detected.

IMPRESSION:  Status post fusion C5-7.  The area questioned on the ___
chest CT is poorly visualized on the current study due to overlapping anatomy.
Given the atypical appearance on both studies, further assessment with a CT of
the cervical spine and cervicothoracic junction is recommended.

PICC LINE PLACEMENT

INDICATION:  IV access needed for antibiotics.

The procedure was explained to the patient.  A timeout was performed.

RADIOLOGIST:  Dr. ___ and Dr ___
performed the procedure.

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right brachial
vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.
Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and immediately after
establishing intravenous access are on file. A nitinol wire, followed by a
0.018 glidewire were attempted to advance into the SVC which was unsuccessful.
A fluoroscopic venogram showed occlusion of the right brachiocephalic vein
with collateral filling of the SVC.These findings were discussed with the team
and a decision to place a midline IV line was made. A peel-away sheath was
then placed over a guidewire and a single-lumen midline catheter measuring 25
cm in length was then placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip
positioned in the right subclavian vein under fluoroscopic guidance.  Position
of the catheter was confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed.  The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Difficult right sided PICC placement due to brachiocephalic vein
occlusion.Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided ___
single-lumen midline catheter placement via the right brachial venous
approach.  Final internal length is 25 cm, with the tip positioned in right
subclavian vein.  The line is ready to use.
